explanation: The king of Israel and son of David, who built the temple in Jerusalem to honor God.
A holy place where people worship and offer sacrifices to God; in this context, the temple in Jerusalem.
A type of tree, especially cedar trees, which were used in building the temple because of their durability and fragrance.
A country in the Middle East, known for its cedar trees, from which the timber for the temple was obtained.
The laborers from King Hiram of Tyre who helped Solomon build the temple by supplying materials and skilled craftsmanship.
A precious metal used abundantly in the temple's decorations and furnishings, symbolizing divine dignity and purity.
An exotic and costly timber, also known as sandalwood, used in the construction and furnishing of the temple.
The innermost room of the temple where the Ark of the Covenant was kept, also called the Most Holy Place.
A gold-covered chest that held the stone tablets with the Ten Commandments, a central element in Jewish faith.
